$comment: Contract for data/tables/polymers.csv. Checked by build/src/schema.js; read by the estimate stage (build/src/estimate/).
title: Polymers
description: The polymer identities the estimate model knows: what a material's base polymer (or a blend) is, as physical facts the model uses where a material publishes none. One row per identity; materials.csv Estimate identity names it. A material whose identity has no row is not estimated, and the build says so.

fields.name: PolymerID
fields.description: The identity, as materials name it: a base polymer (PA6) or a blend (PC-ABS).

fields.name: Group
fields.description: The chemical family the identity's own effect is pulled towards when its data are thin.

fields.name: Morphology
fields.description: amorphous, semicrystalline or elastomer: reinforcement acts differently in each.

fields.name: Melting point °C
fields.description: Typical DSC melting point of the unfilled polymer, used where the material publishes none. It caps heat deflection and, for a polymer that crystallises while printing, drives it.

fields.name: As printed
fields.description: How a semicrystalline polymer solidifies in a print. crystallises while printing: its heat deflection follows its melting point (PA, PP, PVDF, POM). prints amorphous: it crystallises too slowly and deflects near its glass transition (PET, PVA, BVOH). prints amorphous unless fibre-filled: fibres nucleate it in a hot print (PPA). crystallises, not driven by its melting point: PPS printed hot (DECISIONS D56).

enum: crystallises, not driven by its melting point

fields.name: Can crystallise
fields.description: Whether the polymer, or a phase of a blend, can crystallise in a hot mould or on annealing, where a print of it may stay glassy: yes (PLA and PET, which print glassy; the nylons, PP, POM, PBT, PPS, PEEK; a PC-PBT blend through its PBT; a PLA-PHA blend), no (an amorphous polymer, whose bar is glassy however it was made: ABS, ASA, PC, PETG, PCTG, PVB, COC), not known (a class whose products differ or whose makers do not disclose it: a support material, a copolyester sold as CoPE). An undescribed test bar's heat deflection counts only for a polymer that cannot crystallise (headline_definitions.csv Undescribed bar counts for, D177): a glassy bar deflects near its glass transition whether it was moulded or printed, where a crystallisable one's moulded bar can read tens of degrees above a print. Not applicable to an elastomer, which has no heat deflection.

fields.name: Annealing threshold °C
fields.description: The temperature a heat treatment must exceed to change a printed part of a polymer that crystallises when it is annealed: its glass transition, the low end its source prints. Nothing crystallises at or below it, so a value a sheet measured after a treatment there ("annealed and dried at 55 °C for 8 h") is the as-printed part's value: the build judges it as printed and keeps the sheet's words and its typed state (D158). Not applicable to a polymer annealing does not crystallise (amorphous, where an anneal below the glass transition relieves stress and is one) or an elastomer; Not recorded where the row's source has not been read for it.

fields.name: Water uptake
fields.description: high (PA6, PA66, PA6/66, PPA: conditioned modulus about half the dry value) or low (PA12, PA612, PAHT). A conditioned value converts to dry with that class's offset; a polymer with neither reads as dry.

fields.name: Neat density min kg/m³
fields.description: Lower end of the neat polymer's density range. It bounds an unfilled product's density estimate softly, and with the rule of mixtures a fibre-filled one's.

fields.name: Neat density max kg/m³
fields.description: Upper end of the neat polymer's density range.

fields.name: SourceID
fields.description: The source the numbers are taken from, or Not recorded with the Basis saying where they come from.

fields.name: Basis
fields.description: Where the numbers and the classification come from.
